title: Fractional evacuation playbook for composite SLO rollback with economic hysteresis
creator: Priya Rao
description: Implement a staged, fractional rollback controller that uses a composite SLO signal (latency, error_rate, token_cost, throughput) and an economics-aware hysteresis model to determine gradual traffic evacuation and automated rollback actions. The controller should support: cohort-aware baselining, sustained-breach scoring, proportional traffic reduction (fractional evacuation), optionally simulated shadow rewind, and an API for operators to tune sensitivity and cost-weighting. Goal: reduce unnecessary full rollbacks while ensuring user-visible SLOs are protected and unit economics are considered.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a policy configuration that weights four signals (latency, error_rate, token_cost, throughput) and outputs a single composite risk score

When composite risk score exceeds configured thresholds for the configured sustained window, controller triggers a staged fractional evacuation (example steps: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with guardrails
Controller integrates with rollout engine to update route weights atomically and emits events for each fractional step
Operator API allows temporary override and immediate full rollback
Automated tuning job produces recommended threshold adjustments after 2 weeks of telemetry
End-to-end e2e test that simulates a latency spike and verifies controller reduces traffic to target cohort within SLA and records rollback rationale in audit logs
technical_notes: Composite risk uses normalized z-score per metric with per-cohort baselines and a tunable cost multiplier for token_cost
Sustained-breach scoring window default: 3m (configurable); hysteresis implemented as a two-window compare to prevent flip-flopping
Fractional evacuation uses traffic ramp steps with cooldown intervals; each step must pass a health-check before next step
Bayesian posterior monitor used for low-traffic cohorts to avoid noisy threshold breaches; we fall back to frequentist thresholds for high-volume cohorts
Late-arriving tokens and async failures are accounted for by delaying final decision by 1 minute to avoid punishing long tails
design_notes: UX: Rollout console will show a composite risk timeline and suggested evacuation plan; operators can preview the economic impact of each fractional step
Expose an editable policy JSON with fields: weights, thresholds, sustained_window, ramp_steps, cooldown, cost_multiplier
Audit trail must include signal snapshots used to make a decision and the posterior distributions for Bayesian cohorts

decisions: Use composite score (weighted normalized metrics) instead of single-metric triggers to reduce noisy rollbacks
Implement fractional evacuation (gradual traffic reduction) rather than binary full rollback to give systems time to recover and to reduce blast radius
Employ Bayesian posterior fusion for low-volume cohorts to avoid high false positive rates
Include token_cost in composite score with operator-controlled multiplier so cost regressions can be prioritized alongside latency and errors
